claim: The change edits `MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep` from `>=` to `>`. Nothing in REQ-2234 asks for this, and it is a security behaviour change. A graph nested exactly `MaximumObjectGraphDepth` levels deep used to throw `InsufficientExecutionStackException` and is now accepted, so the depth limit (500 by default) effectively becomes limit+1 for all users. The requirement is limited to the analyzer and `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and ledger L12 covers a different depth change.

claim: `DepthStep` changed from `>=` to `>`, an off-by-one that admits one more nesting level than `MaximumObjectGraphDepth`. With the default `UntrustedData` limit of 500, a 501-deep graph is now accepted. A configured limit of N now allows N+1 levels, and a limit of 0 now allows one level. This weakens the stack-depth protection described in L9. It is unrelated to REQ-2234 (analyzer behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration`), and the acceptance criteria require unrelated behaviour to stay unchanged.

claim: Off-by-one change in DepthStep: `>=` became `>`, so the effective maximum nesting depth grows by one. Input nested exactly MaximumObjectGraphDepth+1 deep used to throw InsufficientExecutionStackException and now deserializes. This is a security-relevant behavior change on untrusted data, and it has nothing to do with the analyzer/SuppressSourceGeneration requirement. Users who set a small limit, or who rely on the documented 500 limit, will see different accept/reject behavior without opting in.

claim: The new `continue` on a key-kind mismatch changes generator output for types that mix int and string keys. Previously the mismatched member fell through and was added to the member dictionaries, and the formatter was generated with it. Now that member is dropped from the generated formatter, so the emitted code differs for users who check in or snapshot generator output. The MsgPack diagnostic is still reported, so the build already fails for these types, but the output change is still visible. This is only partly tied to the requirement, which asks for the analyzer to work under SuppressSourceGeneration.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests on a [MessagePackObject] type with one [Key(0)] member and one [Key("a")] member. Compare the generated formatter on base and head. Head omits the mismatched member.

claim: Duplicate [Key] values (int or string) are now silently deduplicated with ContainsKey, so the first member wins and the later one is dropped from the generated formatter. Base threw ArgumentException on the duplicate Add, which the generator or analyzer may have surfaced as a crash. If the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) is reported elsewhere, this is safe. If it is not, a generated formatter can now silently lose a member, with no wire-format error. The diff does not show whether MsgPack006 is always reported before this point.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test on a [MessagePackObject] type with two members both marked [Key(0)]. Assert MsgPack006 is reported and that no exception is thrown. Also run the generator on the same type and check the generated Serialize for the dropped member.

claim: DepthStep changed the check from `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` to `>`. This allows one extra nesting level beyond the configured MaximumObjectGraphDepth, so the limit is off by one on every deserialization path, including UntrustedData. Nothing in the requirement (a SuppressSourceGeneration analyzer bug) or the ledger covers loosening this recursion/depth protection. L12 only concerns a 500 to 5000 change and says to follow the requirement, so it does not authorize this one.
